title: Composition of the ordinary coefficient pullback comparisons
statement: Fix a commutative topological ring B, the specified ring sheaf isomorphism eR, coefficient equivalence G and forgetful compatibility hG. Put W_T = comparisonUpperStar(ModuleCat(ULift B),T) followed by finiteDiscreteCoefficientEquivalence(B,eR,G,hG,T). For scheme morphisms f:S→T and g:T→U and an etale B-module sheaf N on U, W_S.map(Etale.upperStarComp(f,g).hom at N), followed by the canonical ordinary coefficient comparison for f at g* N, then internal f*.map of the comparison for g at N, equals the canonical comparison for f≫g at N followed by internal upperStarComp(f,g).hom at W_U(N). All comparisons are exactly those of [def-weil-pbc-canonical-finite-discrete-pullback]; no derived categories or commutative square are involved.

proof.text: Apply normalized restriction composition. For each coefficient equivalence E, map the inverse-transported restriction comparison through E.functor and express it using the counit, the inverse counit at the source, and the original comparison. Naturality cancels the intermediate counit/inverse-counit pair. This proves composition of inverse-transported restrictions. Apply adjunctionSquareComposition with the coefficient equivalences as vertical adjunctions and the ordinary and internal pullbacks as horizontal adjunctions. Its specified mate identities give pro-etale coefficient pullback composition.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.2 and Lemma 5.4.1; sectionwise coefficient encoding

proof.text: Evaluate the site restriction comparison at an etale object: its map is the identity. The site restriction composition equation reduces to equality of the etale and weakly-etale pullback associators under the inclusion of sites; their underlying scheme morphisms agree definitionally. Apply adjunctionSquareComposition with comparisonAdjunction as vertical adjunctions to obtain the site inverse-image composition equation. Expand the canonical ordinary coefficient pullback comparison into the site comparison followed by the coefficient comparison. Naturality moves the middle site map across the coefficient comparison. Functoriality combines the three mapped site maps; the site composition equation and the pro-etale coefficient composition equation finish the proof.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteDiscreteCoefficientSheafPullbackIso_comp {S T U : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : S ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ U)
    (N : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B))) :
    (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) S ⋙
      (finiteDiscreteCoefficientEquivalence B eR G hG S).functor).map
        ((Etale.upperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) f g).hom.app N) ≫
      (finiteDiscreteCoefficientSheafPullbackIso B eR G hG f).hom.app
        ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) g).obj N) ≫
      (upperStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj B) f).map
        ((finiteDiscreteCoefficientSheafPullbackIso B eR G hG g).hom.app N) =
    (finiteDiscreteCoefficientSheafPullbackIso B eR G hG (f ≫ g)).hom.app N ≫
      (upperStarComp (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj B) f g).hom.app
        ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) U ⋙
          (finiteDiscreteCoefficientEquivalence B eR G hG U).functor).obj N)
